data.about: A simply supported beam carries a uniform load q and two point loads that can slide along the stations. Superposition happens on the load line itself: each strip weighs q·1 m, and where a point load stands its strip grows to q + F — one funicular construction gives reactions, V- and M-diagrams for the combined case. The mirror pole o at the level of the division point l closes the moment funicular exactly on the baseline.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: a simply supported beam A–B, l = 10 m — this time the supports sit at the very ends
steps.title: The beam

steps.caption: left: a uniform line load q = 0.2 kN/m covers the whole beam; the dotted station lines cut it into ten strips of 1 m
steps.title: The line load q

steps.caption: left: two extra point loads F₁ and F₂ stand on the stations (move them with the position sliders!) — their lines of action are dashed
steps.title: Two point loads

steps.caption: right: the ten strips laid off tip-to-tail: a, b, … k — where a point load stands its strip simply GROWS to q + F₁ / q + F₂; all together they span R
steps.title: Superposition on the load line

steps.caption: right: choose a pole o′ on the vertical at distance H to the LEFT of the load line (red segment H below)
steps.title: Trial pole o′ at distance H

steps.caption: right: the eleven rays from the load line to the trial pole
steps.title: Rays a…k → o′

steps.caption: left: from any start FP₀ on the left support vertical, draw each string parallel to its ray, station by station, to the right support vertical
steps.title: The trial funicular

steps.caption: left: the dashed closing line connects the two ends; extending the OUTER strings locates the resultant R of all loads at their crossing
steps.title: Closing the trial → R

steps.caption: right: the parallel to the closing line through o′ cuts the load line at l — the reaction split for q, F₁ and F₂ together
steps.title: Division point l

steps.caption: right: l splits the load line: A = l→a and B = k→l, offset beside it — left: the same forces push up at the two supports
steps.title: Reactions A and B

steps.caption: left: the shear baseline under the beam; V runs from support to support
steps.title: V-diagram — the baseline

steps.caption: left: at A the shear jumps up by A, then falls at slope −q; under F₁ it drops by F₁ — right: the segment l→a
steps.title: V-diagram — jump A, slope −q, drop F₁

steps.caption: left: falling further it drops by F₂ under the second load and the reaction B closes it at the right support — right: the segment k→l
steps.title: V-diagram — drop F₂, close with B

steps.caption: right: place a second pole o at distance H to the RIGHT of the load line, exactly AT THE LEVEL OF l — the closing ray o–l is horizontal
steps.title: The mirror pole o

steps.caption: left: the moment baseline: because o sits at the level of l, the funicular of pole o will close exactly on this horizontal — the dual of the ray o–l
steps.title: M-diagram — the baseline

steps.caption: right: thin rays from the load line to o — left: from the baseline start, strings parallel to them; the polygon returns to the baseline at the right support
steps.title: The moment funicular

steps.caption: left: measure the ordinate y between the grey trial funicular and its closing line at every station
steps.title: Ordinates y on the trial

steps.caption: left: each ordinate scaled by H (× the force scale) and hung from the baseline: the red M-diagram (1 unit :: 1 kNm) — the black funicular is the SAME curve at scale M/H
steps.title: M = H · y

steps.caption: slide F₁ and F₂ along the stations, change their size, q stays — one construction updates reactions, V and M at once; click a kink of the moment funicular for its equilibrium
steps.title: Superposition
